_what: THE DEFECT ENVELOPE, RECONSTRUCTED FROM THE ISSUE — NOT A CAPTURE.
_source: git-bug 1113019, body (#0) and comment #2, both quoting the same live-bench result on 2026-09-01 (session 21).
_honesty: Every field under `envelope` is quoted VERBATIM from the issue. Nothing here is invented and nothing is filled in.

It is NOT the whole envelope: the run was not banked to accept/runs/, and the issue quoted only these fields. Every other key an advance publishes (speed, avg_tps, overshoot_bound, journal_seq, paused_on_exit, ...) is MISSING FROM THIS FILE and was present on the bench.

So this file may be used to prove that a key was ABSENT ONLY for the two keys 1113019 adds — `data.timeout_ticks` and `data.timeout_source` — which cannot have been published, because the code that publishes them did not exist. Absence of anything else here means only that the issue did not quote it.
It is wrapped rather than written as a bare envelope on purpose: a partial capture sitting in accept/runs/ under an envelope-shaped name would be read as a real one.
_note: The map's tick at arm time was exactly 949, so the predicate was TRUE the moment it armed. There is no `timeout_ticks` in the command. The advance ran 187,541 ticks - a bit over three in-game days - and the only thing that stopped it was 722c951's own-faction casualty halt, which had shipped hours earlier the same session.
